rules.body_markdown: This is an exhaustive document detailing the comprehensive Official Rules for *Cyberpunk Trading Card Game (TCG)*.
rules.title: This is an exhaustive document detailing the comprehensive Official Rules for Cyberpunk Trading Card Game (TCG).

rules.body_markdown: This is a reference material, not a teaching one! To learn how to play the game, check out the {[Gameplay Guide >](https://cyberpunktcg.com/gameplay-guide)}.
rules.title: This is a reference material, not a teaching one!

rules.body_markdown: *Cyberpunk TCG* cards are published in multiple languages. English cards, rules, and clarifications are the official versions, and supersede any conflicting texts in other languages.
rules.title: Cyberpunk TCG cards are published in multiple languages.

rules.body_markdown: A game of *Cyberpunk TCG* has two (2) players. Each player is the other’s opponent, or “Rival.”
rules.title: A game of Cyberpunk TCG has two (2) players.

rules.body_markdown: The game constantly checks its own state. It automatically progresses and/or ends the game accordingly. (Win/lose conditions, turn change, etc.)
rules.title: The game constantly checks its own state.

rules.body_markdown: Rules can interrupt to change the game state at any time, even in the middle of effects. They apply automatically as they are relevant, before any effects, actions, or other processes.
rules.title: Rules can interrupt to change the game state at any time, even in the middle of effects.

rules.body_markdown: If you have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area at the start of your turn, you win the game.
rules.title: If you have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area at the start of your turn, you win the game.

rules.body_markdown: The game checks this win condition before the first step of your Start Phase (the Ready Step).
rules.title: The game checks this win condition before the first step of your Start Phase (the Ready Step).

rules.body_markdown: In overtime, if you have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area at any point, you immediately win the game.
rules.title: In overtime, if you have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area at any point, you immediately win the game.

rules.body_markdown: Overtime begins after two consecutive turns in which both players begin with an empty fixer area. (Usually, after both players have completed 7 turns each.)
rules.title: Overtime begins after two consecutive turns in which both players begin with an empty fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: If you already have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area when overtime begins, you win immediately.
rules.title: If you already have seven (7) or more Gig dice in the friendly Gig area when overtime begins, you win immediately.

rules.body_markdown: Winning the game occurs instantly, even in the middle of a game action or effect resolution.
rules.title: Winning the game occurs instantly, even in the middle of a game action or effect resolution.

rules.body_markdown: When you must draw a card from an empty deck (i.e. there are 0 cards in your deck area), you lose immediately.
rules.title: When you must draw a card from an empty deck (i.e.

rules.body_markdown:
If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, the first card you cannot draw counts as drawing from an empty deck. See [Draw](#rule-b07d7e94-c69d-5162-a49c-f77241f8d44b).

> **EXAMPLE:** A card effect says “Draw 2,” but you only have 1 card left in your deck area. You draw the first card, and attempt to draw the second card. The deck is now empty, so you lose immediately.
rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, the first card you cannot draw counts as drawing from an…

rules.body_markdown:
If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

> **EXAMPLE:** According to the rules, you can’t attack a ready Unit, but a friendly Unit’s card text reads “This Unit can attack ready Units.” The card text overrides that rule, so the friendly Unit can declare an attack on a rival ready Unit.
rules.title: If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

rules.body_markdown:
#### RAM Limits

A deck’s 3 Legends provide your deck’s “RAM Limits.” All other cards in your deck must be within these RAM Limits.
rules.title: RAM Limits

rules.body_markdown: By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).
rules.title: By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).

rules.body_markdown: When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.
rules.title: When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.

rules.body_markdown:
A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.

> **EXAMPLE:** A deck with “Goro Takemura: Hands Unclean” (2 Green RAM), “Saburo Arasaka: Stubborn Patriarch” (2 Green RAM), and “Yorinobu Arasaka: Embracing Destruction” (2 Red RAM), has a RAM Limit of (2 Red, 4 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).
rules.title: A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.

rules.body_markdown: Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.
rules.title: Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.

rules.body_markdown: Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition. If a Legend is removed from the game during play, your deck’s RAM Limits are not affected.
rules.title: Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition.

rules.body_markdown: RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.
rules.title: RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.

rules.body_markdown: Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20. These designations refer both to the number of sides on a die and the highest value a die can reach.
rules.title: Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20.

rules.body_markdown: To play a game of *Cyberpunk TCG*, you must bring these items to the table: a 6-set of polyhedral dice, a legal deck of *Cyberpunk TCG* cards, and any other game pieces required by current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: To play a game of Cyberpunk TCG, you must bring these items to the table: a 6-set of polyhedral dice, a legal deck of…

rules.body_markdown: Your 6-set of polyhedral dice must contain one of each: a four-sided (d4), six-sided (d6), eight-sided (d8), ten-sided (d10), twelve-sided (d12), and twenty-sided (d20) die.
rules.title: Your 6-set of polyhedral dice must contain one of each: a four-sided (d4), six-sided (d6), eight-sided (d8), ten-side…

rules.body_markdown: Your dice must be balanced: all of a die’s faces must have an equal chance of occurring on a properly randomized roll.
rules.title: Your dice must be balanced: all of a die’s faces must have an equal chance of occurring on a properly randomized roll.

rules.body_markdown: Numbers on all die faces must be legible to both players.
rules.title: Numbers on all die faces must be legible to both players.

rules.body_markdown: When a die is in play, its current value must be immediately obvious to both players without significant discernment.
rules.title: When a die is in play, its current value must be immediately obvious to both players without significant discernment.

rules.body_markdown: Your dice must follow current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: Your dice must follow current regulations for the game format.

rules.body_markdown: A legal deck of *Cyberpunk TCG* cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.
rules.title: A legal deck of Cyberpunk TCG cards contains 3 Legend cards and a “main deck” of 40-50 non-Legend cards.

rules.body_markdown:
You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name. See [Name](#rule-b311e5d2-a624-5770-a2fa-86d1db7faf78).

> **EXAMPLE:** The Legends “V: Corporate Exile” and “V: Streetkid” are both named “V,” so you can’t use both of them in the same deck.
rules.title: You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name.

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.
rules.title: Your main deck must contain no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards.

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (even if they have different card numbers).
rules.title: Your main deck cannot include more than three (3) copies of a card with an identical name and subtitle combination (e…

rules.body_markdown: Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits. See [RAM & Color](#rule-0667d8bc-c614-55a5-bd7d-ac8f7c6ab606).
rules.title: Your main deck may only include cards within its RAM Limits.

rules.body_markdown: If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.
rules.title: If a card’s effect includes a restriction or exception to these deck requirements, your deck must adhere to that effect.

rules.body_markdown: All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: All cards must be legal according to the current regulations for the game format.

rules.body_markdown: Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.
rules.title: Card sleeves must follow current regulations for the game format.

rules.body_markdown: Both players must complete instructions {7.5-7.9} in listed order before they begin the game.
rules.title: Both players must complete instructions {7.5-7.9} in listed order before they begin the game.

rules.body_markdown: ### Determine which player goes first.
rules.title: Determine which player goes first.

rules.body_markdown:
You and your Rival agree upon and then execute a method to randomly choose a player.

> **TIP:** We recommend both players roll a d20, and choose the player that rolled the higher number. If there’s a tie, both players roll again.
rules.title: You and your Rival agree upon and then execute a method to randomly choose a player.

rules.body_markdown: The player chosen via the random method decides and indicates to their Rival whether they will go first or second.
rules.title: The player chosen via the random method decides and indicates to their Rival whether they will go first or second.

rules.body_markdown: ### Shuffle your main deck.
rules.title: Shuffle your main deck.

rules.body_markdown: You may shuffle by any method you want, as long as it’s timely and properly randomized.
rules.title: You may shuffle by any method you want, as long as it’s timely and properly randomized.

rules.body_markdown: When both players finish shuffling, present your deck to your Rival. Your Rival may “cut the deck” for you, if they choose.
rules.title: When both players finish shuffling, present your deck to your Rival.

rules.body_markdown: Place your main deck in the deck area of your playmat.
rules.title: Place your main deck in the deck area of your playmat.

rules.body_markdown: ### Randomize and place your Legends.
rules.title: Randomize and place your Legends.

rules.body_markdown: Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.
rules.title: Shuffle and randomize your 3 Legend cards with the same randomization method you used for your main deck.

rules.body_markdown: When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival. Your Rival may “cut the deck” of Legends for you, if they choose.
rules.title: When both players finish shuffling, present your Legends face-down to your Rival.

rules.body_markdown: Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.
rules.title: Place all 3 Legend cards face-down in your Legends area.

rules.body_markdown: The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends. These two Legends don’t ready on the starting turn.
rules.title: The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends.

rules.body_markdown: ### Place your Gig dice in the fixer area.
rules.title: Place your Gig dice in the fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: From the bottom up, place your d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and then d20 in your fixer area.
rules.title: From the bottom up, place your d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and then d20 in your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: ### Draw 6 cards.
rules.title: Draw 6 cards.

rules.body_markdown: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand. This is your “opening hand.”
rules.title: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand.

rules.body_markdown: You have up to one (1) opportunity to mulligan your opening hand. The player going first must declare whether or not they will mulligan and if so, complete it, before the second player may declare and execute their own mulligan.
rules.title: You have up to one (1) opportunity to mulligan your opening hand.

rules.body_markdown: After looking at your starting hand (but before the game begins), you may use your mulligan by following these steps.
rules.title: After looking at your starting hand (but before the game begins), you may use your mulligan by following these steps.

rules.body_markdown: Tell your Rival that you’re using your mulligan.
rules.title: Tell your Rival that you’re using your mulligan.

rules.body_markdown: Return your full opening hand to your deck, then shuffle the deck via the same method you used in {7.6}.
rules.title: Return your full opening hand to your deck, then shuffle the deck via the same method you used in {7.6}.

rules.body_markdown: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand. This is your new opening hand.
rules.title: Draw 6 cards from the top of your deck and add them to your hand.

rules.body_markdown: Your turn consists of two phases. It progresses in order: Start Phase, Main Phase.
rules.title: Your turn consists of two phases.

rules.body_markdown: Your turn concludes with an automatic “End of Turn” check after your Main Phase, but before the start of your Rival’s turn.
rules.title: Your turn concludes with an automatic “End of Turn” check after your Main Phase, but before the start of your Rival’s…

rules.body_markdown: When your turn starts, your Start Phase begins immediately. You must take these actions in this order.
rules.title: When your turn starts, your Start Phase begins immediately.

rules.body_markdown: Check if you control 7 Gig Dice. See [GAME OVERVIEW](#rule-0ef7599d-d21e-5efb-bb17-375f7950991c) > [Win Conditions](#rule-8008d6a4-9033-5412-931f-d669c00fade1).
rules.title: Check if you control 7 Gig Dice.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve any start of turn effects.
rules.title: Resolve any start of turn effects.

rules.body_markdown: Remove effects that end “at the start of your next turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Remove effects that end “at the start of your next turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve effects that occur “at the start of your turn,” “at the start of each turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Resolve effects that occur “at the start of your turn,” “at the start of each turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Ready all spent cards in your Legends area, Field, and Eddies area.
rules.title: Ready all spent cards in your Legends area, Field, and Eddies area.

rules.body_markdown: Draw 1. (Add one card from the top of your deck to your hand.)
rules.title: Draw 1.

rules.body_markdown: If there are no cards in this area when you attempt to draw, you lose immediately. See [GAME OVERVIEW](#rule-0ef7599d-d21e-5efb-bb17-375f7950991c) > [Lose Conditions](#rule-6102756a-cd45-50fb-8ded-eea683b79df7).
rules.title: If there are no cards in this area when you attempt to draw, you lose immediately.

rules.body_markdown: “Roll in” a Gig from your fixer area.
rules.title: “Roll in” a Gig from your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: Choose a Gig from your fixer area.
rules.title: Choose a Gig from your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: You may only choose the d20 if there are no other Gigs in your fixer area.
rules.title: You may only choose the d20 if there are no other Gigs in your fixer area.

rules.body_markdown: Roll the chosen Gig. The top face when it stops rolling is its value.
rules.title: Roll the chosen Gig.

rules.body_markdown: Place the Gig in the friendly Gig area, preserving the rolled value.
rules.title: Place the Gig in the friendly Gig area, preserving the rolled value.

rules.body_markdown: After you complete all Start phase actions, the Main phase immediately begins.
rules.title: After you complete all Start phase actions, the Main phase immediately begins.

rules.body_markdown: At any point during your Main phase while you are not taking an action, you may choose to pass your turn to your Rival. When you do, immediately begin the [End of Turn](#rule-5cf5dfb4-f5b3-57c9-b846-99ceef96783e) check.
rules.title: At any point during your Main phase while you are not taking an action, you may choose to pass your turn to your Rival.

rules.body_markdown: During your Main phase, you may take valid Main phase actions in any order.
rules.title: During your Main phase, you may take valid Main phase actions in any order.

rules.body_markdown: Unless stated otherwise, you may take any action any number of times.
rules.title: Unless stated otherwise, you may take any action any number of times.

rules.body_markdown:
### Sell a Card

As an action during your Main phase, you may “Sell a Card.”; sell 1 card from your hand with a Sell Tag in the top-left corner. See [Sell](#rule-6975b781-cb43-5d29-ab97-01954f9127bb).
rules.title: Sell a Card

rules.body_markdown: You may only take the “Sell a Card” game action once per turn.
rules.title: You may only take the “Sell a Card” game action once per turn.

rules.body_markdown:
### Call a Legend

As an action during your Main phase, you may spend 1 €$ to Call a Legend. See [Call a Legend](#rule-5a78278b-9f8b-5e64-b9aa-b2936f705af9).
rules.title: Call a Legend

rules.body_markdown: You may only take the “Call a Legend” game action once per turn.
rules.title: You may only take the “Call a Legend” game action once per turn.

rules.body_markdown: You may also “Call a Legend” during the React Step during your Rival’s turn.
rules.title: You may also “Call a Legend” during the React Step during your Rival’s turn.

rules.body_markdown: When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.
rules.title: When your turn ends, you must resolve any end of turn effects in this order.

rules.body_markdown: Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Resolve effects that occur “at the end of your turn,” “at the end of each turn,” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.
rules.title: Remove effects that last “this turn” and variations thereof.

rules.body_markdown: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, if Overtime conditions are met, Overtime immediately begins.
rules.title: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, if Overtime conditions are met, Overtime immediately…

rules.body_markdown: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, your Rival’s turn begins automatically.
rules.title: When your turn ends, after you resolve any end of turn effects, your Rival’s turn begins automatically.

decisions.interpretation: The two named official demo products are meant for independent play. This alone does not settle all engine policy details.
Exact products have 27 main cards. No general 27-card construction rule is established.
Each exact product has three Legends; 7.3 independently requires three.
If setup precedence is clarified, exact fixed manifests are the narrow candidate authorized by this review; arbitrary substitutions are not established.
7.3 and 3.20 define copy/name/RAM constraints; exact products satisfy these numerically. No waiver or new small-deck construction right inferred.
Product IN ORDER: shuffle deck/Legends then first-player determination. Formal 7.4–7.7: first-player determination then deck/Legend shuffle. No publisher precedence or explicit demo exception found.
Demos specify opposed d20 rolls with ties rerolled; formal 7.5 allows any agreed random method. Existing engine uses uniform seat draw, not simulated opposed d20 rolls.
No preset hand, Legend arrangement, deck stack or scripted opening is prescribed. Ordering between randomizations/first-player selection remains unresolved.

Both products show six-card opening and one optional whole-hand replacement. Formal 7.9 supplies first-player-first resolution; cuts and mulligan order are omitted from reminder rather than explicitly disabled.
D4,D6,D8,D10,D12,D20; choose D20 only after the other fixer dice. No demo waiver.
Ready/draw/roll then MAIN; CALL and SELL once each per turn, CALL also in rival React; Quick and Blocker remain. No sourced Go Solo or Gear-on-Legend exclusion.
Die count, not a Street Cred threshold; first check before Ready.
Rule 1.14 applies; no teaching exception found.

Products explicitly retain sudden death after the second player turn seven. Formal rule uses two consecutive turns beginning with empty fixers. Normal six-die demo progression reaches the same boundary; no claim of a played trace.
User sections 66 and 72 require unresolved official setup conflicts to remain unsupported. Keep references only; no behavior artifact bump.

limitations: No broad corpus refresh or card-mechanics re-review.
PDF visual card counts are captured factual observations, not machine OCR or human-gold certification.
PDF creation date and HTTP deployment Last-Modified are not an authoritative precedence hierarchy.
No source proved a general 27-card construction mode. No legality inferred from collector numbers.
Overtime implementation is a separate full-match blocker even if a deck/setup policy is later admitted.
